On a thoughtful turn, rules for the night crew
This section explains the steps for the whole desk

Companion Animal Travel Desk: service and handoff rules. This section sets the standard for calm handling, clear records, and steady support from booking through pickup.

Staff must review each travel file before contact and confirm that the passenger, the carrier, and the animal details align with the booking note. If a file shows a concern, the first reply should be brief, respectful, and direct. The desk should keep the welcome team informed so boarding support starts with the right plan. When a traveler reports delay, refusal, or a missed connection, the agent should record the facts in full, note any service recovery action, and keep the language plain. <<FACT F110>> If the traveler needs follow-up, the desk should route the case to the supervisor without delay and keep the update chain short.

Animals must be accepted only when the booking record supports the transport request and the carrier appears fit for use. Staff should check for secure latches, clean bedding, and enough room for the animal to stand and turn in a natural way. If a passenger arrives with a pet in poor condition, the agent should pause the process, bring in the supervisor, and avoid promise-making before review. The desk should never guess at an outcome or tell the traveler that a case is settled until the record is complete.

Communication should stay steady and courteous at every handoff. Agents must use the same facts in each note, avoid side comments, and pass only the details needed by the next team. If a traveler sounds worried, the agent should listen carefully, restate the issue in simple terms, and set the next step without delay. The desk must also keep the welcome team aware of any change that could affect boarding, loading, or pickup.

For exceptions, service gaps, or any animal welfare concern, contact the senior coordinator or the shift supervisor at once.
